Feature: Is there an overt marker for the absolutive?
curated_comment: Confirmed value 0. Absolutive is zero-marked in Lepcha. -nun~-nu is the ergative/ablative marker on A arguments; S and O are unmarked. Source: Plaisier 2007:127-129.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging on first person pronouns?
curated_comment: Confirmed value 1. 1sg pronoun go takes -nu in ergative function: "go-nu taso Pyok ma-zuk-ne" (1S-ABL yesterday work NEG-make-NEG, ex.241); "go-nu hudo-sa...taPyukup-re-m" (1S-ABL...hit-PRF, ex.242). Source: Plaisier 2007:128.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging on second person pronouns?
curated_comment: Confirmed value 1. 2sg pronoun ho is the standard form; -nun~-nu applies to transitive subjects of all persons per the general description (Plaisier 2007:127-129). Ex.239: "ho taso ka-sa...ngol-do h'-nu..." (2S yesterday...) in a temporal context, consistent with person-general ergative. Source: Plaisier 2007:127-129.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging on third person pronouns?
curated_comment: Confirmed value 1. 3rd person NPs and pronouns take -nun~-nu in ergative function: "kaju-nun Pong-re-m tsuk ma" (dog-ABL boy-DEF-DAT bite AST, ex.240); "hudo-sa daughter-ABL...buk ma" (3S-GEN daughter-ABL hit AST, ex.243). Source: Plaisier 2007:128.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging on full NPs?
curated_comment: Confirmed value 1. Full NPs (animate) take -nun~-nu as ergative: "kaju-nun" (dog-ABL, ex.240), "Dorji-nun" (proper noun-ABL, ex.28 p.62), "muro-nu" (man-ABL, ex.30 p.62), "Palyu-nun-do" (cat-ABL, ex.36 p.65). Source: Plaisier 2007:62,65,128.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the imperfective aspect?
curated_comment: Confirmed value 1. -nun~-nu is less likely with imperfective/non-completed events but can occur. Plaisier (2007:128-129) states the marker is conditioned by "completedness of the event" as one of several factors — it is not categorically excluded in imperfective contexts. Source: Plaisier 2007:127-129.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the perfective aspect?
curated_comment: Confirmed value 1. Ergative -nun~-nu is most strongly associated with perfective/completed events. Ex.240-243 use assertive particle (AST) and perfective verb forms. Plaisier (2007:128): "more likely to occur in the past tense because the agentive meaning... is more likely to be appropriate in contexts where the activity has already actually taken place." Source: Plaisier 2007:127-129.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the past tense?
curated_comment: Confirmed value 1. Past tense is the prototypical context for ergative -nun~-nu: "kaju-nun...tsuk ma" (dog bit, AST), "go-nu...taPyukup-re-m" (I hit, PRF). Plaisier (2007:128): "-nun~-nu is more likely to occur in the past tense." Source: Plaisier 2007:127-129.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in non-past tenses?
curated_comment: Confirmed value 1 with caveat. Ergative -nun~-nu is less likely in non-past tenses but is not categorically excluded. Plaisier (2007:128): "the ergative suffix is more likely to occur in the past tense" — implies it can also occur elsewhere. As an optional, probabilistic marker, GB409_9=1 is retained. No direct non-past example verified from the grammar. Source: Plaisier 2007:127-129.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the indicative mood?
curated_comment: Confirmed value 1. All attested ergative -nun~-nu examples are in indicative declarative clauses (assertive particle ma, perfective forms). Source: Plaisier 2007:127-129.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in non-indicative moods?
curated_comment: Value 1 retained. -nun~-nu is described as a case clitic applicable to animate transitive subjects generally; no restriction to indicative mood is stated. Direct examples of non-indicative moods (imperative, subjunctive) with nominal ergative were not found in the ergativity section (Plaisier 2007:127-129). Source: Plaisier 2007:127-129.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the realis status?
curated_comment: Confirmed value 1. All ergative examples are realis declaratives. The animacy, transitivity, and completedness conditions all favour realis contexts. Source: Plaisier 2007:127-129.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the irrealis status?
curated_comment: Value 1 retained with caveat. -nun~-nu can theoretically occur in irrealis contexts as an optional marker, but Plaisier (2007:128) notes it is less likely when "the activity has not yet been completed," which includes future/hypothetical contexts. As an optional marker, its possibility in irrealis is not excluded. No direct irrealis example verified. Source: Plaisier 2007:127-129.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the context of an agentive A?
curated_comment: Confirmed value 1. Ergative -nun~-nu marks volitional agents: "kaju-nun...tsuk" (dog bite, ex.240), "go-nu...zuk" (I make, ex.241). Plaisier (2007:129) lists "volition on the part of the subject" as a conditioning factor favouring -nun~-nu. Source: Plaisier 2007:127-129.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the context of a non-agentive A?
curated_comment: Confirmed value 1. -nun~-nu also marks the instrument or cause of an activity. Plaisier (2007:127): "-nun~-nu likewise marks the instrument whereby an activity is performed or may indicate the cause of an activity or state." Non-agentive A (instrument/cause) takes the same suffix. Source: Plaisier 2007:127.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the context of a topical A?
curated_comment: Confirmed value 1. Topical agents take -nun~-nu in the attested examples (e.g., "kaju-nun" in ex.240 where dog is the discourse topic). No restriction on topical A is mentioned. Source: Plaisier 2007:127-129.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the context of a non-topical A?
curated_comment: Confirmed value 1. Non-topical agents also take -nun~-nu (e.g., "muro-nu" man-ABL in ex.30 p.62 where the man is backgrounded; "Palyu-nun-do" cat-ABL in ex.36 p.65). No topicality conditioning mentioned for the ergative marker. Source: Plaisier 2007:62,65,127-129.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the context of an animate A?
curated_comment: Confirmed value 1. Animate A is the primary context for -nun~-nu: Plaisier (2007:127): "Lepcha -nun~-nu is used when an animate agent and an animate patient are linked by a transitive verb." Animacy of the subject is an explicit conditioning factor. Source: Plaisier 2007:127-129.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the context of an inanimate A?
curated_comment: Original value 1 is incorrect. Plaisier (2010:127-129) explicitly states that animacy of the subject is one of the key factors conditioning -nun~-nu: the marker is used "when an animate agent and an animate patient are linked by a transitive verb" and the factors include "animacy of the subject." Inanimate A arguments do not receive ergative marking in Lepcha. Corrected to 0. Source: Plaisier 2010:127-129.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in main clauses?
curated_comment: Confirmed value 1. All primary ergative examples (ex.240-243 pp.128) are main declarative clauses. Source: Plaisier 2007:127-129.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in non-main clauses?
curated_comment: Confirmed value 1. Ergative -nun~-nu appears in non-main clauses: ex.28 (p.62) "Dorji-nun zuk-tho" (Dorji-ABL make-EXH) is a relative clause head ("the house that Dorji built"); ex.30 (p.62) "muro-nu zuk-tho-bu" (man-ABL make-EXH-FCT) is a factitive embedded clause; ex.31 (p.63) "munju-sang-nu...dun-Pam-ba-re" (grandmothers-ABL tell-PRG-when) is a temporal subordinate clause. Source: Plaisier 2007:62-63.

Feature: Is ergative alignment of flagging conditioned by any other factor?
Comment: There is marking of A in a construction with a transitive verb wtih two animate arguments (one agent, one patient), which, if compared to a prototypical intranstivie construction, creates an ergative-absolutive alignment. However, there is marking of the agent regardless of the transitivity of the verb, i.e. there is marking of A and S (when it is more prototypically agentive); in this case, it would not form an ergative-absolutive alignment.
curated_comment: Confirmed value 1. Ergative -nun~-nu is conditioned by multiple factors: (1) animacy of subject, (2) volition of subject, (3) degree of control, (4) transitivity of verb, (5) completedness of event. Plaisier (2007:129) explicitly lists all five as conditioning factors. Source: Plaisier 2007:127-129.

Feature: Are the ergative and the genitive expressed by the same marker?
curated_comment: Original value was empty. Based on Plaisier (2010:127-129): the ergative marker is -nun~-nu (ABL suffix in dual function), while the genitive is expressed by -sa (visible in Ex.242: hudo-sa "3S.OBL-GEN" and Ex.243: hudo-sa daughter-ABL). ERG and GEN are expressed by distinct morphemes. Value set to 0. Source: Plaisier 2010:127-129.

Feature: Are the ergative and the instrumental/comitative expressed by the same marker?
curated_comment: Confirmed value 1. -nun~-nu is the Lepcha ablative suffix repurposed as ergative AND as instrumental/comitative marker. Plaisier (2007:127): "marks the instrument whereby an activity is performed." Ergative and instrumental/comitative are expressed by the same marker -nun~-nu. Source: Plaisier 2007:127.
